tips.comment: Olly Murphy's 6yo gelding had a bit in hand when he landed a handicap hurdle by 2 lengths off a mark of 128 at Cheltenham last time out in an impressive performance, as he was worth more than that winning margin would suggest. This hugely progressive horse (he beat Gowel Road, winner of the Cleeve, in a handicap (also at Cheltenham) in December) is a big player in this heat.
A 5-time career winner who has won all the last 3 starts, including over this CD last time out. Carries an 8 lbs penalty today but won going away last time and has a big chance again today.

Ran to form second, four and a half lengths in a handicap hurdle here latest where he had the run of the race. Won't get an easy lead today, but blinkers for the first time and steadily progressive. That run will put him right in the mix each way.

Topgun Simmy looks interesting for Shark Hanlon in this 3m Handicap at Haydock. He has won 2 of his 7 starts over hurdles. The second win came on Monday at Down Royal, where he showed his liking for good ground. He has a 7lbs penalty in a deeper race, but at these odds, he looks a good each-way bet with 4 places on offer.

Zain Nights was still going well at Cheltenham last time when he made a mistake 2 out behind Long Draw, who is favourite here. He won this race last year and is only 7lbs higher, and he seems to have a preference for flat left handed tracks and good ground, so he has his ideal conditions today.
My Bobby Dazzler is closely handicapped with a few better-fancied rivals in this race. Finished 2nd here last May and looks a huge each-way price in an open-looking race.
Ki Woo looks very progressive. He has won his last 2 races in impressive style and could still be ahead of the handicapper after his easy win at Bangor last time out.

Porter in the Park has a couple of seconds to his name in this grade and was successful at Ludlow latest. He makes appeal over this distance on a sound surface despite being up in the weights. Top jockey booked for the ride.

The upcoming two-mile handicap chase marks the beginning of the prestigious jumps season. Our Champ emerges as the leading contender, particularly well-suited to the good, drying ground. His impressive victory at Ascot last November showcased his ability, and he has maintained consistent form ever since, despite trainer Chris Gordon's earlier struggles last season. Encouragingly, Gordon has recently seen a turnaround, securing two winners. While Our Champ's latest run at Plumpton demonstrated his competitive spirit, he may have exerted himself too early. Success at Haydock, however, will require jockey Freddie Gordon to show patience in what is expected to be a large field. Conditions appear favorable, and the long, flat straight should complement Our Champ's running style. The track has been watered but is expected to dry as the day progresses, further improving the ground.

Dance and Glance has run really well returning from wind surgery with a win (beat the smart Fasol a neck at Taunton) and second (to Bareback Jack where he encountered trouble in running and is better handicapped now). Anthony Honeyball (SR 17%) trained and Harry Cobden (SR 33%) is an eyecatching jockey booking for that stable. Selection of five (of 14) tipsters on the Racing Post card. Won two and placed in all three other hurdle starts. Low in the handicap here, carrying 10 stone 7 pounds. Major player.

Not a favourite horse of mine, but the fact the O'Neill 8yo has dropped 13 lb in 18 months prior to winning last month at Newcastle, his first win since Jan 2022, can't be ignored. He wore cheekpieces for that win for the second time. He ran well when he first wore them at Cheltenham's Showcase meeting last October and retains them for today.

Comes into this race with plenty to prove at present, but currently sits 3 lbs below his last winning mark, with Sean Bowen booked to ride. He ran a decent enough race in this event last season, finishing a clear 2nd behind runaway winner Pickanumber, beaten 15L albeit. That was off a mark of 121. He runs off 117 this time but doesn't get the assistance of a 7 lbs claiming jockey this year. I still feel Sean Bowen is more than value for the 3 lbs comparing jockeys, so that doesn't concern me. He managed to win off a mark of 120 nto, winning a class 4 handicap off top weight easily, beating Man Of The Sea comfortably, with just over 4L separating them at the line. Admittedly, he's not shown much since then. His mark has slidden 9 lbs, however, which should help on that front. With that solid run in this race last term still in mind, he looks a solid frame contender if repeating the dose.

I like the profile of Goblet of Fire here. Some might see him being a 5yo as a negative, but progressive 5yos have won 2 of the last 8 runnings of this, and if they're good enough, then they're old enough. He's been raised 5lb since his debut as a 5yo last time out, which appears to prove that the horse has taken a huge leap forward. He was an easy winner that day and gets almost identical ground and trip here. Considering that he needed the run on seasonal debut last year, that run can be upgraded, and there could well be more to come.

Ooh Betty was a half-length 3rd in the Scottish Champion Hurdle at Ayr and is one of the few in this lineup who has good form in Group races. Was also 3rd in another Group 2 race at Ascot in January. Usually runs over today's distance and very much likes the going. Usual jockey Ben Jones is riding for Ben Pauling in this race, and Rex Dingle takes over, but I wouldn't be surprised if there is a change of jockey as it looks like Ben's ride is a non-runner.

Give Me Five has raced twice at Haydock, resulting in a first and second finish. He won over course and distance in his last outing by just under a length. Today he is five pounds higher. In his last two races, he has been sent off in front and never allowed anyone to pass. If again using those tactics, he should once again run well.

Has been running well enough of late, hitting the frame at a slightly lesser level. There is lots of pace on here which is going to be a help to him as a hold-up performer. Might be capable of a stronger effort if things drop right in front of him.

Welsh Charger is having his first run at this course but considering his running style , this galloping type of course should suit. The selection ran well in defeat at Ayr last time out which is more of a tighter course than this , i feel Haydock will be more suitable. His recent runs were on softer ground conditions , ground conditions will be faster today but he had some decent form on good ground at the start of his career. Eachway tip for Welsh Charger.
Glory And Fortune looks good value at 16/1. Oldest horse in the race at 10. Won last time out at Chepstow 15 days ago and will wear cheekpieces tomorrow. EW NAP 5 places.

An 8-time career winner, 6 times over jumps and twice on the flat, winning a chase over 2 miles at Chepstow on penultimate start back in February. Has since run really well when staying on 5th in a fast-run Premier handicap chase at the Aintree Festival last month. Reverts back to hurdles here off a 5 lbs lower mark and looks an each-way player with 5 places.

LUNAR SOVEREIGN is interesting down at the foot of the weights. He has previously been pitched into deeper more competitive races than even this Swinton Hurdle renewal and he could be ready to peak third-up for this spell. With Brian Hughes aboard he could surprise.
Jules Winfield was held up for an impressive win in a bumper at Ballinrobe 29 days ago and Mr Derek O'Connor comes over to ride him again for Tony Martin.
The stable does well with NH Flat horses and has only had one runner this season, a winner of a bumper at Market Rasen last month. So, this horse merits respect today at an each-way price.

Magellan Cloud heads to Haydock after a promising third at Musselburgh on seasonal return. That run suggested he’s progressing nicely, and the step up to a mile should suit. Drawn well and with Jason Hart aboard, he’s got a solid chance of building on that effort.
Kirkdale returns to Haydock after a decent fourth at Southwell last month, where he shaped as if the run would bring him on. He’s back on turf now, off a mark of 77 and he could be sharper this time.

Mostly campaigned on all-weather without too much to shout about, but followed up a 3-length defeat in class 2 company with a 25/1 winner in class 4 at Southwell. Only nudged up 3lb after winning by half a length, with the 3rd place by 5 lengths. Claiming jockey retains the ride and is raced in class 4 company. Should continue good form back on turf.

A former course and distance winner and a winner over this trip on the Southwell tapeta in February 2025. All 4 subsequent races have been over further, most recently over a mile and a quarter at Lingfield on the polytrack last month. This drop back to 7 furlongs is of interest.
9 of 10 wins have come on the all-weather, including 2 of the last 4 starts. Returns to turf on a workable mark and holds an each-way chance.

We had a previous nice price winner with Nubough dead-heating in the week, and now I'm hoping lightning strikes twice with another big odds victor going in again. VINCE LE PRINCE has won for us nicely previously and returns to the turf perfectly well handicapped if matching the run at Musselburgh the run before last. Nudged down in the weights and avoids the middle of the stalls, so could get involved.

My NAP today comes in the (flat) feature at Haydock this afternoon with ALYANAABI at 2/1. Tiber Flow can be opposed given Caravaggio tend to need their first run of the year (1/35, A/E 0.29) and his son has looked rusty on his two starts off a break previously, meanwhile Kikkuli carries a poor FlatStats rating with F Marsh booked who brings a damning 2% SR (A/E 0.22) in Spring on runners who ran 57+ days ago. The M Appleby yard is yet to climb out of their slump (1/41, A/E 0.22 this season) and I don’t expect that to change here given their historic 2% SR (A/E 0.47) with outsiders in Spring. Array is yet to show he’s up to this level on quick ground. Alyanaabi won the Gr3 Tattersalls in 2023 and has ran well in behind smart performers such as City Of Troy, Notable Speech and Rosallion since. The O Burrows team have started the season in flying form (6/10, A/E 2.78) so I’d expect their charge to by fully wound up for the Spring Trophy and Shadwell’s impressive 75% SR (A/E 1.82) with favourites dropping in class who finished 7th or worse LTO adds further confidence.
Could be a gimme for group-winning Tiber Flow here against a field of less established horses. Has run over course and distance here too.

Has the benefit of a recent run, unlike the rest of this field, having raced over this trip at Thirsk 28 days ago. Entitled to come on for that run and could use that race sharpness to good effect here.

Giselle runs at Lingfield for the first time out this season. This Frankel filly won her maiden well at the Curragh and then was a decent 3rd in a Group 3 at the Curragh over a mile in her final run last year, where she was carried left when challenging and was promoted to 3rd from 4th by the Stewards.

The ground at Lingfield is quick following recent watering, though the course remains a challenging test for runners. In the 1:50 race, the selection is Gincident, from James Owen's stable. Having shown promise in previous outings, he is considered well-handicapped after his transition from Richard. Ideally, he would benefit from a smaller field and fast turf, but the presence of front-runners could provide jockey Hector Crouch with opportunity to maximise his performance.

Dashinwhitesargent won twice last season off a mark of 73, including over this distance on good at Epsom. Only one pound higher, he could go close as long as he can find a decent position from his wide draw.
Lightly raced 4-year-old French import. Two UK runs and a little unlucky to lose by a neck two weeks ago over this 10-furlong trip. Good RPR rating posted. Room for improvement.
Mister Daydream won at Hamilton on good to firm ground on his latest outing, now bids for a hat-trick. Carries 5lb for the win but has a progressive profile. Leading chance with strong momentum.

A 6-month break has worked well in his favor in the past, and he has won 2 of his last 3 runs. However, there was a poor effort last time out when he finished only 10th of 11 at Nottingham last November. But he has bags of ability, so it's not surprising that his mark remains unchanged.
He won at Brighton by 5 lengths a month ago over the same trip, and even with a 7lb penalty, he still looks progressive and should be able to land another win this afternoon.
Previously with the Aidan O'Brien stable, still partnered with Ryan Moore here, in what could be a tactical race, this could be a good bet.

Aidan O'Brien dominated the Trials at Chester this week, and his Puppet Master looks likely to do the same at Lingfield. He won a maiden at Galway last August and has since finished 4th in Group races at Newmarket and Leopardstown. He should benefit from the step up to 1m3.5f, and with Ryan Moore booked, he looks the most likely winner here.
Did well to win on his second start after a promising debut at Newmarket last year. Related to Dubai Millennium from the dam's side, suggesting he will improve with experience. Good each-way chance.

Rahibb stands out as a strong contender for the upcoming one-mile race, bolstered by his recent impressive form and the expertise of jockey Sylvester De Sousa. With a commendable 17% strike rate and recent victories, he appears fit and primed for competition. His runner-up finish at Haydock further highlights his potential, particularly if he can secure an early lead on fast ground.

Was impressive winning at Wolverhampton back in March of this year, which is impressive because that is one of the trickier AW courses. Was still competitive LTO at Southwell last month. Going up in class makes life harder, but can be in the mix if improvements are made.

Only raced twice as a 2yo winning well here on debut before a cracking run in the Group 3 Oh So Sharp on final start. The winner that day hasn't set the world alight on sole run since but the third Flight has just given the tip top Desert Flower a real scare in the 1000 Guineas at Newmarket last weekend. Form sets the standard here and looks value to me against some exposed sorts. Trainer is a dab hand at improving his 3yo fillies no end and if fit this potentially smart sort looks a good thing in this. Holds plenty of fancy entries including the Irish Guineas, The Oaks and the Coronation Stakes at Royal Ascot so would want to be putting these away if genuinely up to that level. Only 3yo in the field and getting all the weight allowances surely wins this.

The 4yo filly was beaten in a £238K US Grade 1 four weeks ago, not much going right for her in the race. She was a runner-up in Group 1 last summer and followed that with a Group 3 win. The return to quick ground will be a big positive for the selection in this Group 3 contest.

Ran well to win over today's trip at Wolverhampton in March when returning from five months off and followed up with a close second (by a head) over the same trip at Southwell last month. Should be thereabouts.

Just five career runs for the 3yo. He was 3rd in a good AW handicap during January, and he should be ready for his return to turf after a 3-month break. Two runs on quick g/f turf going conditions in the first half of last year, winning a 15-runner maiden contest - both the 3rd and 4th from that race are now rated 100+. He was then a close 4th of 13 in a novice stakes while giving weight away and was badly hampered at a vital time, beaten by two runners now rated 88 and 99. His handicap mark of 77 looks very attractive.

Showed bits and pieces of form in Ireland and wasn't far off them on her debut for this yard. Cheekpieces return which could be a help and won't be inconvenienced by a return to turf. A sharp seven should be ideal on the grass.

6yo gelding Bang On The Bell has won his last race over 5f at Windsor. Is up 4lbs for that but only 1lb higher than when runner-up in this race last year. Should make another bold bid and the double here today.

Maharajas Express has been running well and comes into this in decent nick with a couple of wins and solid placings. He’s back at a track he’s handled before, Probert takes the ride, and if he gets out well, he should be in the mix again.

The system just throws up ITS TIM today. A bit like yesterday's winner Zappata, this one has the double whammy of seemingly still being ahead of the handicapper and looking like there's nothing here that'll come close.
9-time winner whose recent form has been disappointing, but if rediscovering some of past form, will have an each-way chance.
3yo irish gelding Solar Biricz was a good 3rd of 11 lto over 5f at Beverley. Drops in class today and will be in the mix.

Lost by a neck 10 days ago off a mark of 53, losing to a horse now rated 61. That was off quick ground and thee ground matches to that today. Dreambird Dolly runs off 55 today and has the plum draw of stall 1, which should suit her preference of leading. William Carson takes the ride again, who knows the horse well and has hope of breaking her duck.

FEAR AND FAST drops in grade and now comes back to Nottingham a full 7lbs lower than when narrowly beaten here last November (on soft going, but seems versatile going wise). Some disappointing runs to start off the campaign, but there's possibly some untapped potential in this one. If the new visors help, then maybe we've got one that turns the corner at a tasty price.
Well proven against peers in this class and a very smart run behind Trilby at Beverley last time suggests that this horse could be a good selection here.

Eased 2 pounds in the official ratings and of interest dropping in trip and grade after racing in a Class 3 over 7 furlongs at Southwell 13 days ago, with the first-time cheekpieces offering the potential for improvement too.
Shamrock Bay appeals as it has won twice. No headgear reached for (i.e., not a nutter), and gelding may allow for better settling overall. Great chance.

First View comes back to the UK after a solid run in Dubai, where he wasn’t disgraced in a deep handicap. He’s now 2lb below his last winning mark on turf and has gone well fresh before. If he handles the return to softer ground and gets a good pace to aim at, he looks fairly treated and capable of getting involved.

KING OF CHARM gets the trip, going and grade, whilst also having previous for running well fresh. Probably this price because of the last time out flunk at Chelmsford last winter, but was drawn wide and can be excused. 3lbs above last winning mark but got close from higher in the weights at Newmarket when last seen on turf, so looks a dangerous one to rule out too readily.

Masar gelding who won two of his five starts on good to firm ground on turf last year at this level. He has been held in both of his two starts since a 165-day absence, which came in tougher C3 races. He should be ready to roll third time up today. He is down in class, and he is now 1 lb below his last winning mark, so he is in with a shout here.

Harswell Ruby stayed on well to get his head just in time at Doncaster and looks good value to follow up against a short-price favorite. That was after a short head defeat on turf, so she's clearly in good form and will likely have a big say in this race.
Doubt connections expected this horse to be running off a mark in the 60s when they purchased this horse. It looks a very workable mark for a very good stable. Each way chance here.

Race 5 at Nottingham today is the Handicap (Class 5) for 3-year-olds over 1,677 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 3-year-old gelding Seed Investor from the Ivan Furtado yard, and will be ridden by Tom Eaves. This son of Coulsty was desperately unfortunate not to have opened his account last time out when trying this distance for the first time, beaten by a head. He can easily atone for that in this field and should go close.
A winner at 1m on all-weather. Third of 13 behind Bulletin, only beaten two lengths on the latest outing at Southwell over 1m last month. Solid each way NAP.

MINI MAC comes back to Nottingham 2 lbs lighter than a mid-division finish here the run before last, so he's considered if back in that sort of mood here. Didn't have a clear run then, so I marked it up a bit on re-watching. It's therefore surprising that he's this price at the time of writing, as there are each-way claims for sure.

South Parade is in rude form, and he will break off and try to make all in this race. I can't see any challengers with the necessary speed to overhaul the selection. Richard Fahey has a great record here and can add to his tally.
Haymaker has threatened for a while on a dangerous mark, and I'm hoping that this course and distance winner can get his head in front again.
Will strip fitter following 2 runs last month after a 4-month absence. Led inside the final furlong but was headed close to home over 6 furlongs 12 days ago. The drop in trip appeals.

BURNING CASH probably needed the run last time out after a lengthy time off track, and is potentially well weighted to get involved from a big price here. Now drops to much lighter in the handicap than last summer's showings and if coming on from the seasonal debut, he could outrun these odds. Those runs were in much tougher company too.

Kode Secret had a pipe opener recently and he can take this race in his stride. Easterby and Kirrane have hit a purple patch recently so confidence is high. The selection won twice last May and may repeat the feat this year.
Celestial King impressed so much in the Craven Breeze Up Sales that he commanded a monster record price of 1.75m Guineas by Amo Racing. He could outpace Military Code in receipt of six pounds.

Military Code made a sharp debut at Newmarket, winning over 5f with a strong finish. He carries a 6lb penalty here, but with experience on his side and Buick staying on, he’s the one to beat. The Godolphin colt is bred to improve and could be Royal Ascot-bound if he delivers again.

Two return runs for the 4yo filly. Beaten just over a length last week in a Listed contest despite meeting plenty of trouble in the race. She was beaten by three runners rated 105+. She should be a big player in this handicap while racing off a 94 mark.

Very much a group filly in handicapper's clothing. Class above this lot. 2nd in a messy Listed race when last seen in August. Only had 3 runs as a 2-year-old, winning twice, and is expected to be much better at 3.
The best runs of Zapphire last season came on good to firm going. She will appreciate conditions at Ascot, and Holly Doyle takes over the ride from her usual apprentice rider, Tom Kiely-Marshall.
Went third close to home over the extended mile at Nottingham 11 days ago. Remains on the same mark and won this race last year off a 7-pound higher mark.

The model I run has simulated this race and suggests Roarin Success is the value bet here. This result has largely been driven by Roarin Success having the highest RPR of the field, but goes out carrying the second lowest weight over this 1m trip on good ground. This horse is a prior course and distance winner, and the trainer has a high RTF%.

Really tricky Victoria Cup and almost impossible to find the right selection. However I'll take a chance on 4yo irish colt Roi De France. Is in good form with a 3rd and a 2nd in his two runs this season. The drop back to 7f and return to turf should suit and he definitely is one of the better horses in this field. Should be in the mix.

I had a saver bet on this one in the Irish Lincoln and he ran a cracker when well backed to finish 5th after travelling well and fading late on. I like that form as a few have run well since including the winner Orandi who was just beaten two smidges in the real Lincoln at Doncaster. Lightly raced sort for a 5yo who only made debut last March beating another good sort in State Actor who was runner up in the Irish Cambridgeshire since. Has good form over 7f on decent ground so I'm expecting a huge run here from a decent draw and Hollie Doyle has been booked. The English handicapper may well of underestimated this improving sort who looks to have ideal conditions and has form that stacks up well.

Ten Pounds has been on a roll, winning four of his last five, including a tight finish at Newmarket last month. He’s up 3lb for that but still looks progressive and has a strong record in big-field handicaps. If he keeps improving, he should be right in the mix.

Qirat has gone up the weights for finishing 2nd in two competitive handicaps at the end of last season. Both came off proper soft ground, and I think a return to a quicker surface, as well as 7f, will suit him best. He won on reappearance last year and boasts plenty of Ascot form. All the pace looks high, but it should give him a good tow into the race from stall 9, and he can claim this from a mark of 99 before moving onto pattern company as a 4yo.

This horse just keeps progressing and progressing as the quality of the races improves and he still doesn't look like he's reached his ceiling yet. The jockey rode a great race on him last time and keeps the ride, he looked like he was always confident whilst not winning by far and a 4lb rise looks well within his compass. That win made it 5 from 6 for the horse at this trip and he looks cracking e/w value at 9/1.

Metal Merchant is a lively outsider. He ran below form last time but usually has good course form. He is capable of bouncing back to place. MM is a solid contender despite a below-par seasonal return. He won the Spring Cup last year and has strong course form, including a fourth in the International over this track. With fitness likely improved, he could sneak into a place with decent odds.

Mick & David Easterby can take this year's renewal of the Victoria Cup this afternoon with Diligent Resdev, who was a comfortable winner of last year's Ayr Bronze Cup, winning going away by nearly two lengths off a mark of 79 in the hands of a 7 lb claimer. Last month, he was a solid staying-on third at Musselburgh, off a six lb higher mark.

English Oak was slowly away on his first run this season and probably would have needed the race anyway so it could be a good prep for this race. He has been dropped 2 lbs and his trainer Ed Walker is in flying form. He runs well at Ascot and likes these big fields so looks worth a chance.

A replacement for a non runner, and Hickory I thought was of small interest here following a yard switch. He went well in this last year off 4lbs higher, and perhaps more interestingly comes here fresh. He put up a career best RPR on reappearance last season before his 4th in this, so perhaps coming here fresh could see him go even better. He’s 3/5 a place over course and distance, lightly raced for his age and seemingly hard to win with, but hopefully his lowest career weight carry can see him outrun his odds.

Popmaster has a proven track record at Ascot, having finished a close second in this exact race last year. Notably, he's 2lb lower in the weights this time, which could give him the edge needed to go one better . While his recent form has been mixed, he showed promise with a third-place finish at Lingfield in February. His familiarity with Ascot's unique challenges and his ability to perform well in big-field handicaps make him a strong contender. With his course experience and a favorable weight, Popmaster offers solid each-way value and is poised for a strong performance.

The market is struggling to separate Qiraat and Roi De France here but I think both can be opposed; the former carries his highest-ever handicap mark and I’m not convinced he’ll cope with it on quicker ground, meanwhile RDF has to overcome the Gosden’s 11% SR (A/E 0.49) withe fancied runners over 7f at Ascot. Gleneagle Bay carries a poor FlatStats rating so is unlikely to offer much value and Ten Pounds is up to a mark of 102 off a neck success LTO. It makes sense to take an each way price here and of those METAVERSE makes the most appeal at 16/1 (5 places). The son of Starspangledbanner put his reappearance run behind him LTO at Kempton, winning by 1l at Kempton and probably having more in the tank than appeared. The 6th (Supreme King) was a head 2nd in a C3 handicap at Chester this week from a less than ideal draw so the form holds potential plus the booking of H Davies is a huge positive given his start to the season (19% SR, A/E 1.35) and 50% SR (A/E 2.82) when riding for D Menuisier.

Silver Sword, Dylan Cunha trained grey, is nicely drawn high in stall 17. Reached a high handicap mark of 103 early in his career. Has continued to run well and seems better handicapped now on a mark of 92 (8 stone 11 pounds here). Winner at Meydan back in March. Respectable efforts in big handicaps the Spring Cup and Suffolk Stakes in recent weeks. The drop to seven furlongs is strange (usually a held up performer needing every yard of a mile) but intriguing. Kieran Shoemark takes over in the saddle. A big price at 40-1 for a classy horse, now well handicapped.

Going through a barren run as it's now been 15 runs since the last win back in 2023. But it helps he's a C&D winner and should welcome the dropped mark. I hope course experience has a positive impact tomorrow.

A 6-time career winner, 5 times on the AW and once over this trip at Newmarket last May in a good time on the clock. The stable had an impressive winner here yesterday, and this horse could run well at big odds.

Turquino is unexposed. Ran quite green in two starts in March on the all-weather for Andrew Balding but still maintains an unbeaten record managing to win the first quite comfortably and both with a good bit in hand. Will need to improve to continue the 100% record but fancied to do so. This doesn't look very strong for a Class 3 contest. Oisin Murphy (SR 23%) rides.

Probably still won with a bit in hand at Leicester last time and seemed to relish the quick ground when others won't. Trainer Dylan Cunha is starting to get winners, and it's eye-catching that William Buick takes the ride.
Eddie Greaterex reappears to ride Mighty Bandit again after he towed them along for most of the way before tiring late. He should go better with a weight pull and a bit sharper now. Only ride.

Joined Archie Watson from A.P. O'Brien in January 2025. Two runs for the new yard over a mile and a mile and a quarter have followed. Will strip fitter for those two races following an absence of 299 days. Tries this mile and a half trip for the first time, and the latest run suggested it will suit going third towards the finish.

At the price, I think HOUSTONN could be worth a small each-way punt. Although he carries top weight, he does have a few things in his favor, especially the conditions. He won over 1m2f last summer before two runner positions, including at this track. 14/1 is a tempting price with extra places available.

Interesting and open race, and a chance taken on Night Breeze who is up in class here off two big weight carries and finds himself down the bottom of the weights for this. 4/5 a place at the trip, 3/4 a place in this class, 1/1 on the going, he’s also 4/6 a place going right-handed. He’s a decent bit of pace to latch onto on his inside, and he’s entitled to take a step forward for what was close to a career-best effort last time. Down a lb, I think he can get competitive at a nice enough price.
Appears to be a bit of a low handicap mark achieved for this horse, who cost nearly half a million, making this an attractive play in this race.

The model I run suggests Chartwell Jock can win this one. The race simulation has Chartwell Jock coming in first ahead of Cape Breton in second and Kokanee in third. This result has largely been driven by Chartwell Jock having the highest RPR of the field, but is well treated off the weights (carries a mid-range weight). Steps out in stall 6 for this 1m 1f trip, which is helpful. Oisin Murphy picks up the reins, who is in great form.

Had three all weather runs as a 2yo and probably showed best form on last run when staying on well over a mile at Wolverhampton last back end. Made a mockery of handicap/seasonal and turf debut at Beverley last month when winning readily bouncing off the good ground. Looks progressive and handled the step up in trip well too and in fact is the only distance winner in the field. Willie Buick booked and looks a fair bet to me so hopefully we'll be having a right old Kokanee 'knees up' when this one bolts up and hopefully backs up some confident picks today.
Poor run last time out after a long break, coming 8/8 at Newmarket over 1m 1f. Upped in trip and the extra furlong looks to suit. Top jockey booking.
Whisper, a 7-year-old chestnut mare, is now with Alan King. This slow starter hasn't won since May 2nd, 2023, but this isn't a particularly strong race. Worth a small bet.

Over an inadequate 7f on seasonal debut, this horse goes back up in trip. Her sole win came on quick ground at Nottingham, and she’s gone well on the AW off 8 and 9lbs higher than this mark adjusted for claim. Mason Paetel looks worthy of his 7lbs, and is 11/19 a place with 5 winners for this trainer in the last year. A small field scenario could suit as hopefully if she misses the break she won’t become too detached, and indeed has made all in the past.

Arnaz heads to Ascot today after a strong seasonal return at Haydock, where he was narrowly beaten in a big field. That form has been franked since, and with William Buick booked, he looks well-placed to go one better.
4yo gelding Smart Vision is on a good mark just 2lbs above his last winning mark from last August. Was a good 3rd of 11 lto over 6f at Doncaster and drops in class today. Should be in the mix.
Often flatters to deceive, but with 4 places on offer here and at least consistent, you'd hope this horse can place here.

Ran well to win over today's trip at Wolverhampton last month and wasn't beaten far when finishing seventh from twelve when dropped back to 5f at Chelmsford three weeks ago. Step back up in trip should suit. Hollie Doyle in good form recently. Should be involved at the finish.

It clearly showed LTO that he had been off for 6 months when 10 of 10 at Leicester last month. So expecting a much better effort tomorrow, which is helped by a dropped mark, and hopefully the use of blinkers does the trick.
Showed what he is capable of when winning at Brighton last month. Now, the net mark with the 3lb claimer matches the last winning mark, so anything is possible if improvements are made.

The 33-1 about bottom weight Jackson Street might be as good an angle to take to this race as any. Four years old, a Dandy Man colt, full brother to the smart AW performer Lord Of The Lodge, so potentially has ability. Formerly with Karl Burke and Dylan Cunha, gained first win (off OR64) over six furlongs at Newcastle in December. Poor on first outing for Michael Attwater back in January (ran very keenly) but has been given a decent break and from OR67 at the foot of this Class 4 handicap could easily come back primed for a big run. Can't be ruled out.

4yo gelding Jimmy Speaking is back on his last winning mark which was here over C&D exactly a year ago. Jockey Oisin Murphy is booked for the first time which is another plus and he will be in the mix.

Was well beaten over 7f at Musselburgh last month when returning from almost eight months off but wasn't beaten far when finishing second when dropped back to today's trip a fortnight ago. His two career wins have been over today's trip. Should be thereabouts.

The model I run suggests Last Outlaw is the value bet here. Steps out with the highest RPR of the 12-runner field. One of the younger runners here, so would be looking for progression, being less exposed. Tries the tongue tie for the first time. Kieran Shoemark picks up the reins. Stepping out of stall 3 is helpful over this shorter 6f trip.

Strike has never really convinced on an all-weather surface, so it was no surprise on his debut this season 33 days ago when he finished 4th of 13 over 7f. He should strip fitter for that, and the return to turf and the drop back to 6f should suit. The yard is in form, and Rob Hornby has won on him twice before, both over today's trip and both with the ground on the fast side. He looks overpriced and makes plenty of each-way appeal.
7yo gelding Counsel is in great form with form figures of 1123 in his last 4 races. The booking of amazing Rossa Ryan is a big plus and he should be in the mix here with his prominent run style.
Twice a winner last year, who finished 2nd in 2 races following that last win before disappointing when last seen in October. Holds an each-way chance if finding best form on return to action.

Spanish Star is ten years old now but makes some appeal on first seasonal start. Trainer Patrick Chamings (SR 18%) is in decent form. The horse has run really well in better races than this on his last two seasonal openers. Struggled last season but this handicap mark of 75 is nine pounds lower than when last seen on turf in October last year. Could be very ready to go after a break and worth a play for the win at 20-1 in a 12 runner race.

The model I run suggests the value bet here is Scots Poet. Scots Poet has the highest RPR of the field here in what looks like a pretty open race. By far the lowest official rating leaves this horse well treated by the handicapper, and he steps out carrying 10 lbs less than the current market leader.
Good ground could be in Dream Jet's favour here at Hexham. 3 places on offer in a 7 runner race with a lot of firms. Danny McMenamin takes over from Craig Nichol in the saddle.

Point winner Famous Liss was made favourite for his first chase here last month, but he made an early mistake and unseated his rider. He runs again off the same mark of 105, and with a clear round, he could win. 13-2 are decent odds for his first win under rules.

He won over course and distance in June, and despite finishing 3rd in a couple of subsequent starts, he returns here 3 lbs lower than his last winning mark. His two runs this calendar year have been poor but have been in too high a class and he drops to a Class 4 today.
Winner from this mark over hurdles not so long ago and ran well over fences at Sedgefield last time. Stays well and still looks capable of improving with this only his 4th run over fences.

River Of Joy comes with risks attached in the 4:40 at Hexham tomorrow - first time over fences and stamina to prove - but I really liked the belated reappearance third over hurdles at Ffos Las. It’s an awful long way to send a runner for just a prep, with the stable banging in the winners too.
All 3 wins over fences came at this track over 2m4f. He attempts 3m today; however, he placed over 3m in a point-to-point earlier in his career, and he is now 2lbs lower than his last winning mark.
Prolific point winner Wallace Olinger goes for a maiden hunter chase at Hexham and with a clear round he should make no mistake this time.

She has already won 3 point-to-points, including over course and distance in 2023, with her most recent coming last time out. She should continue in her rich vein of form and looks far too big in odds based on that.

Up 5lb, a repeat of the CD win 26 days ago would appear to be enough. Ewan Whillans yard is in fine form & his lightly-raced 5yo should have more improvement in him, particularly as he goes up in trip.

He has placed in 3 of his 5 runs over course and distance, as well as having wins at Cartmel, Sedgefield, and Kelso. He is still 8 lbs higher than his last winning mark. However, he has been running well off similar, including a 2nd in a Class 2 series finale at Kelso on his penultimate start. Today, he drops into a Class 4, so he should still make his presence felt.

Ambassador ran well on good ground in a Class 4 on penultimate start that showed strong signs of returning to form and is now back below last winning mark. In class 5 again back he looks like one that will be trying hard and well capable of being bang there come the business end of the race over 2m4f and with such a low weight. Take into account riders claim and this looks winning opportunity. Forgiven forlast run when never put into the race.
Has been disappointing in the last 2 races, having unseated at Aintree in May last year and pulling up at Ayr in March. Has dropped to a competitive mark and holds an each-way chance.

She won her most recent point to point start in November and hails from a very powerful yard. She is a half sister to high class bumper winner Ballycasey so in this field today, she should be able to run well.

The model I run suggests Celestron Star can win this one. It has the highest RPR of the field and goes out carrying a reasonably similar weight to the rest of the field (i.e., not being penalized for having more potential). Luke Scott on board claims a further 5 lbs, and hopefully, this gives Celestron Star the edge over this 2m trip.

Ideal Guest reappears after a decent back-to-form 2nd last time out, where the first-time hood brought about the improvement, and it is being applied again. So, I expect more improvement. I expect the race to be run at an even pace throughout, so this will give the selection the opportunity to front run and get a stride or two on the challengers.

Edvard Grieg could be another winner for in-form trainer Dylan Cunha. He has been a bit inconsistent since joining the trainer from Ireland. He does have bits of form that should see him winning races, and with his handicap mark down over a stone since his first run for the Cunha yard, plus the first-time blinkers, he could finally break his maiden tag.

Antiphon was a beaten favorite last time out at Windsor and now drops in class. It is fitted with a visor for the first time, looking to try and recover losses incurred there. Very well handicapped to achieve a successful conclusion.

Unfortunately, there is nothing heroic about his current record, which reads as only one win from 18 runs and now 17 runs since that win back in 2022. He finished 13th of 13 at Thirsk LTO last month, so big improvements are required. But a big drop in mark gives him a chance.
Certainly expensive to follow if you backed it every time, but if you followed the horse at this official rating level, its form tells a different story.
Has had excuses for last two runs, he is the value against the two hotpots and is overpriced in my opinion. At least he stays the trip!
Have been waiting for this one to run since it was backed off the boards last time out but then declared a non runner. Not a bad return at Thirsk. 8lb below his last winning mark.

How's The Guvnor has had two runs for a new handler, both modest runs on the AW. Previously with Clive Cox, it showed ability for Cox, with best efforts being on turf on GD or GF going. The switch back to turf could see the needed improvement for this horse to get competitive.

TOUCHWOOD blows hot and cold, but it can't be denied that there's potentially a solid run in him at this price. Not seen much on turf but considered now down in grade and weights from last season's showings. Will probably be dropped in but should have a good pace to aim at and could get involved.

Has finished 2nd twice in 5 starts to date, including on the latest outing over this course and distance in April. That form looks good in the context of this race and has every chance of going 1 better.

Candonomore returns to Leicester after a tidy win at Wetherby, where he came from mid-pack to score by 1½ lengths. He’s up 4lb for that but still looks fairly treated off 76. With a good draw and David Allan back aboard, he’s got a solid chance of following up if the race sets up for a late run.

Won over this trip in Class 5 grade at Brighton on penultimate start. 9th of 10 when upped in grade to Class 4 over the extended mile at Epsom last time out. The ease back in grade to Class 5 appeals.
Kept on when 4th of 11 over a mile at Pontefract at the end of last month and this step up in trip will suit.

The model I run suggests Serious Chat should win this race. Goes out with the highest RPR of the field. Charlie Maggs on board claims 5 lbs, which helps bring the weight being carried back down to the mid-range from the higher range of this race. Decent prior first and looking to build on that here.
Doyen Quest looks past the post, and he should win this without coming off the bridle. On a day when it looks so very, very difficult, a winner is a winner. It could mean success while others fail.

The model I run suggests the value bet here is Calagogo. Doyen Quest is expected to win, but there is virtually no market for this. If anyone is betting on a horse race with odds of 1/14, they need a serious risk management lesson. The next best option here is Calagogo and looks next best to step up should anything unexpected happen to Doyen Quest.

The model I run suggests Moonlight Artist should win this race. Moonlight Artist steps out carrying the highest RPR of the field, the second lowest official ranking, and subsequently has a reasonable amount of weight to carry compared to the other runners. Moonlight Artist is a previous course and distance winner here, and also has the second highest top speed on the card.

The model I run suggests Cobbler's Boy should win this. Cobbler's Boy has by far the highest RPR of this field but is not penalized for it in the weights. All horses except one go out carrying the same weight for this 2m trip. This is Cobbler's Boy's first run since a recent wind op, and this should show further improvement. He also goes out with the tongue tie on for the first time, which should aid concentration.
Big Boy Barney had 2 runs in bumpers and performed okay. Might need a longer trip, but it might be worth backing against the Skelton odds-on favorite.

I'm going for the outsider in this 4 horse race - Mammies Boy. He was a close up 4th last time out behind Tarahumara but he was blocked in terribly everywhere he turned and just couldn't get a clear run. Now here upped into a class 4 he returns at Warwick with that run under his belt, which I'm sure would of blown off the cobwebs and he will strip fitter for that run. He has 10st 4lbs on his back now as Benjamin Macey takes off a nice 7lbs as well. The outsider of the 4 could go well.

The model I run suggests Emerald Time is the value bet here. Emerald Time steps out with the highest RPR of the field but carries a manageable mid-range weight over this 2m flat hunt race. 108 days since the last run would give me a slight pause for thought and is something to be aware of.

Only a short head separated First Approach from Award Ceremony when they met on the all-weather at Dundalk last month. First Approach appeared to finish the better of the two that day without doing enough to get to the front. With that experience and this time running on turf, taking First Approach to register his first win.

Albert Einstein is a 2-year-old son of Wootton Bassett ex Yet, who herself was placed at Group 2 level. He makes his racecourse debut here in this extended 5f race where he's drawn 5/9 on this straight course. He'll be ridden by W Lordan for Aidan O'Brien & Coolmore. A win here will book his ticket to Royal Ascot. The stable is in top form this week with four winners at Chester. I make him my Nap of the day.
The favorite (as of writing) looks to want further on pedigree, so happy to take on with this more speedily bred horse, for top Keane/Lyons combo.

Ex won a bumper and won on hurdles debut on penultimate start. Form was boosted when the 3rd home won next time out. Selection turned out on the flat 2 days later and just failed, having got headed close to home. Back to hurdles today and should go close under the penalty.
Two bad mistakes in his last two races cost him any chance of winning. Cost him a place last time and possibly the win on the penultimate start. Has an each-way chance if jumping better.
The form of her 4th is strong. She will enjoy the better going on offer here and has a nice draw. The one to beat.
P Twomey could not be in any better form, and his stats here at Naas are superb. He sends just the one runner out today in Bond International, ridden by Billy Lee. I expect a very good run.
Placed in 2 of 4 starts last year and made a pleasing reappearance at Naas in March. Likely to be better for having had that run and holds an each-way chance.

Leading Endeavour won a point last year but was beaten big distances in her first 4 starts in maiden hurdles. There was a big improvement on handicap debut at Ballinrobe last time when she was 3rd of 12, beaten just 2 lengths. The step up to 2m5.5f and good ground clearly helped, and this extended 3 miles could bring more improvement. She looks a good each way bet with 5 places on offer.
Disappointing run last time, but looked a threat on the penultimate start when brought down 2 out when having every chance. Pedigree suggests that this step up in trip should suit.

Backonthegoagain is a 7-year-old gelding trained by Colin Bowe. He is 0-5 under rules and has posted a lowly career-best RPR of 89. Yet, the Irish handicapper took no prisoners by setting an opening handicap mark of 102. Disappointing in the first two handicap hurdles on soft and heavy ground, but today's return to good ground could suit him. Having won two PTP on good and good to yielding ground over 3m, he could potentially be well handicapped now off 93 with Aidan Kelly taking off a valuable 5lb. Given the fact he heads the weights suggests this is a very weak handicap, and at the price, Backonthegoagain, out of an unraced dam related to two jumpers who won four races each, could well surprise.

FREE PARKING has had an interrupted career , but could be sharper for his reappearance run and he has been given time potentially to find a suitably weak handicap hurdle. This is a sole entry today for ace dual-purpose trainer John McConnell and claiming conditional Alex Harvey arrives with his confidence high. Bred to appreciate this more extreme test of stamina from his reduced mark he merits a market check.

The good odds are the main reason I'm placing this tip, risky because a fair bit of improvement will be needed. Probably found the 2m3f distance too sharp last time when finishing 9th of 17 , did leave the impression further would be better so 3miles today may be more suitable , this horse did do well at this distance in point to points earlier in his career. Very small eachway tip.

DIPPEDINMOONLIGHT has won a NH flat race and a point-to-point race at 2m 2f and 3m. She was third in a Listed NH flat over a 2m race at Gowran Park on her latest outing in October last year. Over hurdles today, the course, distance, and going should suit, and she could well be able to win this race.
Cameletta Vega is a bumper winner last seen in a hot Grade 2. Well beaten but was against strong opposition. Previously won on similar going, and stepping up in trip could suit. Big potential.
Kalixa looked very taking in the maiden win over course and distance last time. Bred from classy Aga Khan lineage, has to be on it.

Some big guns here in this, but I'll chance another trainer that does well here. He only has the one runner in Gotomylovely, which has a previous win under its belt and is bred for a longer distance than that win. Good each way.

Annarubyrose is a 4-year-old filly trained by Gavin Cromwell. She makes her bumper debut and is a first foal out of an unraced dam who was out of a dam that won four times on the flat and four times over hurdles, posting a career-high RPR of 137. So, fairly useful. Gavin Cromwell has picked up 20 bumpers in recent years and seemingly has his yard in good nick with his last three runners going 2-2-1. Hence, Annarubyrose is my short-priced banker of the day.
Showed plenty of promise on bumper debut last month when finishing 8th of 16 at Ballinrobe. Improvement likely, and that gives an each-way chance.

Lightly raced 4-year-old who won well over 6f at the Curragh on first handicap start just 5 days ago. Carries a 9 lbs penalty but is open to lots more improvement and may well just follow up with a top rider in the saddle.
Twice a winner in May last year but has been off the track since October. The ground may not be ideal for return but holds an each-way chance if finding last year's form.

IMPROVE YOUR MOVE may have wintered well and could be favourably tretaed ahead of her handicap debut. One noteworthy run in France before joining trainer David Marnane and this yard do well with sprint handicappers. Never an issue getting one ready either , so the market can help us today.
A 4-time winner whose last win came over this CD last December. Has been running consistently well and looks to have a big chance in what looks like a fairly weak event.

Tannery Park has better form on the flat than over hurdles, but he definitely has potential and is interesting here. He has never been closer than 5th over hurdles but was placed on the flat at both Ballinrobe and Tramore last summer. He returns to hurdles 1 lb lower than his last run and looks a good each-way bet with 4 places on offer.

NOBLE HILLTOP runs for a yard who have plenty of their handicappers well supported since landing a huge punt recently. This stable appear to be able to improve mature types this season in particular and maybe this mare will be the subject of another market move.

This could easily blow up in my face, but at a current price of 40/1, I can’t overlook Mark Roper’s newest recruit 7-year-old French Mare IDOL. She likely needed the outing here at Cork (24f, Soft) 20 days ago, having been off for 248 days and making her debut for the yard. A Daughter of JUKEBOX GLORY, she’s bred to appreciate quicker ground & return to sounder conditions could be key. Her standout piece of form came three starts back at Kilbeggan (19f, Good/Yielding) in a competitive Class 3 last July, finishing fifth, 17 lengths behind THE WALLPARK ??' no disgrace. More notably, she was just ¾ of a length behind CHAMPELLA, who has since landed two Class 3s off marks of 116 and 126. The 123-rated THE BIG CHAP also finished behind her that day. IDOL also won a bumper for Willie Mullins on her only start for powerhouse yard, so clearly has some latent talent. She now lines up off 105 ??' 2lbs lower than that strong Kilbeggan effort and gets a further 7lb pull with Ross Berry booked. This will demand a leap of faith, but there’s just enough in her profile to warrant a speculative nibble. VERY Small stakes only.
